Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)

40 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Seared Marinated Chicken

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken thigh, boneless skinless120g240g360g480g
Plain yogurt30g60g90g120g
Ginger-garlic paste5g10g15g20g
Lemon juice5ml10ml15ml20ml
Kashmiri chili powder¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Neutral oil1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Butter15g30g45g60g
Onion, chopped40g80g120g160g
Tomato passata100g200g300g400g
Cashews, raw10g20g30g40g
Heavy cream20ml40ml60ml80ml
Garam masala¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Kasuri methi¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Sugar½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Saltpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp

Steps

  1. Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and mix with yogurt, half the ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, and half the Kashmiri chili powder. Marinate at least 20 minutes.
  2. Sear the marinated chicken in hot oil 3-4 minutes per side until golden with charred spots. Set aside — it will finish cooking in the sauce.
  3. Melt half the butter and cook the chopped onion 4-5 minutes until soft and see-through.
  4. Stir in the remaining ginger-garlic paste 30 seconds until fragrant.
  5. Add tomato passata, cashews, remaining chili powder, and a splash of water. Simmer 8-10 minutes until deep brick-red and oil separates at the edges.
  6. Blend the sauce until completely smooth (let it cool first), then return it to the pan.
  7. Return the seared chicken to the pan and simmer 8-10 minutes until no pink remains inside.
  8. Stir in the sugar, remaining butter, and cream until the sauce turns lighter orange-red.
  9. Crush the kasuri methi between your fingers and sprinkle it in with a final pinch of garam masala. Simmer 2 more minutes.
  10. Taste, adjust salt and cream, and serve hot with basmati rice or naan.

Dal Tadka (Yellow Lentil Dal)

35 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Tempering the Spices

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Split yellow lentils (toor or moong dal)50g100g150g200g
Water (for cooking dal)250ml500ml750ml1000ml
Turmeric¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Saltpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp
Ghee1 tsp2 tsp1 tbsp4 tsp
Cumin seeds¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Asafoetida (hing)pinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp
Garlic, sliced1 clove2 cloves3 cloves4 cloves
Dried red chili1234
Onion, chopped20g40g60g80g
Tomato, chopped30g60g90g120g

Steps

  1. Rinse the lentils until the water runs mostly clear, swishing and draining 2-3 times.
  2. Bring the lentils, water, turmeric, and a pinch of salt to a boil, then simmer on low, lid slightly ajar.
  3. Cook 20-25 minutes, skimming foam, until the lentils are completely soft and mushy.
  4. Whisk the cooked dal until creamy and slightly thick, like a hearty soup.
  5. Heat the ghee until a cumin seed sizzles right away when dropped in.
  6. Add cumin seeds, dried chili, and a pinch of asafoetida (hing), sizzling about 15 seconds until toasty, not black.
  7. Add garlic 30 seconds until light golden, then onion 3-4 minutes until soft and browned at the edges.
  8. Add the chopped tomato and cook 2-3 minutes until soft and pulpy.
  9. Pour the sizzling tadka into the pot of dal, stir it in, taste for salt, and top with cilantro before serving.

Chicken Biryani (Hyderabadi-Style)

75 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Layering Rice Over Chicken

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Basmati rice75g150g225g300g
Chicken thigh, cut into pieces130g260g390g520g
Plain yogurt30g60g90g120g
Ginger-garlic paste5g10g15g20g
Red chili powder¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Garam masala¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Saltpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp
Crispy fried onions15g30g45g60g
Mint leaves, chopped5g10g15g20g
Cilantro, chopped5g10g15g20g
Ghee1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Bay leaf1234
Green cardamom pods2468
Cloves36912
Cinnamon stick (small)1234
Saffron threads + warm milkpinch + 1 tbsppinch + 2 tbsp¼ tsp + 3 tbsp¼ tsp + 4 tbsp

Steps

  1. Marinate the chicken in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, half the garam masala, and salt for at least 30 minutes.
  2. Rinse and soak the basmati rice 20-30 minutes so the grains cook up long and separate.
  3. Boil water with bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and salt seasoned like seawater.
  4. Add the drained rice and cook uncovered 5-6 minutes until about 70% cooked, then drain immediately.
  5. Sear the marinated chicken in hot ghee 2-3 minutes per side until lightly browned.
  6. Spread the seared chicken across the bottom of the pot.
  7. Layer the partially cooked rice on top like a blanket, without stirring it in.
  8. Sprinkle fried onions, mint, cilantro, remaining garam masala, and saffron milk over the rice.
  9. Cover tightly and cook on very low heat 25-30 minutes without lifting the lid — this is the 'dum' steaming step.
  10. Rest off heat, still covered, 10 minutes, then fluff and mix gently from the bottom up before serving.

Chana Masala (Chickpea Curry)

30 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Blooming the Spices

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Canned chickpeas, drained150g300g450g600g
Onion, chopped40g80g120g160g
Tomato, chopped60g120g180g240g
Ginger-garlic paste5g10g15g20g
Cumin seeds¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Ground coriander½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Ground cumin¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Turmeric¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Red chili powder¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Chana masala spice blend½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Amchur (or lemon juice)¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Neutral oil1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp

Steps

  1. Heat the oil and let the cumin seeds sizzle about 10 seconds until toasty.
  2. Add the onion and cook 5-6 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden-brown.
  3. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste 30 seconds until fragrant.
  4. Add the ground coriander, cumin, turmeric, and chili powder, stirring 20 seconds to bloom the spices.
  5. Add the tomato and cook 5-6 minutes, mashing it down, until it turns thick and jammy.
  6. Add the chickpeas and water, stirring to coat every chickpea.
  7. Simmer, partly covered, 10-12 minutes until the sauce thickens and the chickpeas soak up flavor.
  8. Stir in the chana masala spice blend and amchur, then simmer 2 more minutes.
  9. Sprinkle with cilantro and serve hot with rice, roti, or naan.

Paneer Tikka Masala

40 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Searing Marinated Paneer

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Paneer, cubed100g200g300g400g
Bell pepper, chunked30g60g90g120g
Onion, chunked (for searing)20g40g60g80g
Plain yogurt (marinade)20g40g60g80g
Ginger-garlic paste5g10g15g20g
Kashmiri chili powder¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Garam masala¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Neutral oil1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Butter (gravy)10g20g30g40g
Onion, pureed (gravy)30g60g90g120g
Tomato passata (gravy)80g160g240g320g
Cashews (gravy)8g16g24g32g
Heavy cream (gravy)15ml30ml45ml60ml
Sugar¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Kasuri methi¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Saltpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp

Steps

  1. Cut the paneer, bell pepper, and onion into similar-sized chunks.
  2. Mix yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, and half the garam masala into a marinade. Gently toss in the paneer and vegetables. Marinate 15-20 minutes.
  3. Sear the marinated paneer and vegetables in a single layer, 2-3 minutes per side, until charred and softened. Set aside.
  4. Melt the butter and cook the gravy onion 4-5 minutes until soft and see-through.
  5. Add tomato passata and cashews, simmering 8-10 minutes until deepened and thickened.
  6. Blend the sauce smooth (cool first), then return to the pan.
  7. Stir in the cream, sugar, and remaining garam masala until the sauce turns soft orange.
  8. Add the seared paneer and vegetables back in, simmering gently 3-4 minutes, stirring softly so the cubes stay whole.
  9. Crush the kasuri methi over the top and stir in.
  10. Taste, adjust salt, and serve hot with naan or rice.

Kerala Fish Curry

35 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Tempering Mustard Seeds & Curry Leaves

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
White fish fillet (tilapia, cod, or snapper)130g260g390g520g
Coconut milk100ml200ml300ml400ml
Turmeric¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Saltpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp
Red chili powder½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Ground coriander½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Fenugreek seedspinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp
Mustard seeds¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Curry leaves6121824
Shallot, sliced30g60g90g120g
Tomato, sliced30g60g90g120g
Ginger, julienned5g10g15g20g
Garlic, sliced1 clove2 cloves3 cloves4 cloves
Tamarind paste½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Coconut oil1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp

Steps

  1. Pat the fish dry and rub with a pinch of turmeric and salt. Set aside.
  2. Heat the coconut oil and add the mustard seeds — they'll pop and crackle within seconds.
  3. Add the fenugreek seeds and curry leaves, frying about 10 seconds until fragrant and slightly crisp.
  4. Add shallot, ginger, and garlic, cooking 3-4 minutes until soft and light golden.
  5. Add the remaining turmeric, chili powder, and coriander, stirring 15 seconds to toast without burning.
  6. Add the tomato and cook 2-3 minutes until it softens and breaks down.
  7. Pour in the coconut milk and tamarind paste, bringing to a gentle simmer, not a hard boil.
  8. Slide the fish into the curry in a single layer, cooking gently 6-8 minutes until opaque and flaking apart easily.
  9. Taste and adjust salt or tamarind, then serve hot over steamed rice.

Lamb Rogan Josh

90 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Browning the Marinated Lamb

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Lamb shoulder, stew chunks150g300g450g600g
Plain yogurt30g60g90g120g
Kashmiri chili powder1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Ground fennel½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Onion, sliced40g80g120g160g
Garlic, minced2 cloves4 cloves6 cloves8 cloves
Ginger, minced5g10g15g20g
Bay leaf1234
Green cardamom pods2468
Cinnamon stick (small)1234
Cloves2468
Ghee1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Water100ml200ml300ml400ml
Saltpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp

Steps

  1. Mix the lamb with yogurt, Kashmiri chili powder, and ground fennel. Marinate at least 30 minutes, or overnight.
  2. Heat the ghee and sizzle the bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves about 20 seconds until fragrant.
  3. Add the onion and cook 6-8 minutes until deep golden-brown, lowering heat if it browns too fast.
  4. Add the garlic and ginger and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
  5. Add the marinated lamb and cook 5-6 minutes until the outside turns gray-brown all over.
  6. Pour in the water, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
  7. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer, lid ajar.
  8. Simmer 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lamb is fork-tender.
  9. Taste and adjust salt. Fish out the whole spices before serving hot with rice or naan.

Gulab Jamun (Bonus)

45 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Frying the Dough Balls

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Full-fat milk powder30g60g90g120g
All-purpose flour5g10g15g20g
Baking soda⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Ghee, melted5ml10ml15ml20ml
Milk (to bind dough)10ml20ml30ml40ml
Sugar (for syrup)60g120g180g240g
Water (for syrup)60ml120ml180ml240ml
Cardamom pods, crushed1234
Rose water¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Oil or ghee for deep fryingas neededas neededas neededas needed

Steps

  1. Make the syrup first: boil sugar, water, and crushed cardamom until dissolved, then simmer 5 minutes until slightly syrupy. Stir in rose water and set aside warm.
  2. Combine milk powder, flour, and baking soda in a bowl.
  3. Rub in the melted ghee until the mixture looks like damp sand.
  4. Add milk a little at a time, kneading gently into a soft, smooth dough.
  5. Roll the dough into small, smooth, crack-free balls.
  6. Heat oil to medium-low — a pinch of dough should sink, then slowly float back up.
  7. Lower the balls into the oil a few at a time, never crowding the pot.
  8. Fry gently, rolling often, 6-8 minutes until deep reddish-brown all over.
  9. Slide the fried balls directly into the warm syrup while still hot.
  10. Let soak at least 30 minutes before serving warm or at room temperature.
